{{.heading_1}}

The "Cash Out" Tool: Standard lenders are slow. They often say "No" to broken chains, unmortgageable properties, or auction purchases. Bridging lenders say "Yes"—but they charge a premium for that speed. This calculator reveals the true cost of "Retained Interest."

Most bridging loans use Retained Interest. You don't make monthly payments. Instead, the interest for the year is deducted from the loan at the start. This confuses many borrowers because the loan amount you "get" is much lower than the amount you "borrow."

{{.heading_2}}

The actual cash you need in your hand today.
Bridging is priced monthly (0.75% pm ≈ 9% pa).

{{.heading_3}}

Typically 2% of the gross loan amount.

{{.heading_4}}

To put £200,000 in your bank account, you must borrow the higher amount below. The difference is the "Cost of Speed."

£0 Paid upfront
£0 Added to loan

prose_blocks:
The Reality Check: Always Have an Exit

Bridging lenders do not check your income. They check your Exit Strategy. If you cannot prove exactly how you will pay the loan back in 12 months (e.g., "Sell Property A" or "Refinance to BTL"), they will not lend.

The "Default Interest" Trap:
If you go 1 day over your 12-month term, the interest rate often doubles (e.g., from 0.75% to 2.5% per month). This destroys equity rapidly. Never take a bridge without a solid Plan B.
